content.title: About
content.content: French onion soup is a classic French dish made from caramelized onions, beef or chicken broth, dry white wine, and aromatic herbs. It is traditionally served with toasted baguette slices topped with melted Gruyère cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally the soup is cooked in earthenware pots that are presented under a flaming sugar crust.
The first French onion soup recipes appeared in Parisian cookbooks in the 18th century.
The dish became popular among workers and students because of its simplicity and inexpensive ingredients.
Gruyère cheese used for gratinating gives a characteristic golden crust and rich aroma.
In some regions a splash of cognac or brandy is added to deepen the flavor.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Onions contain quercetin and sulfides that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports immune system
items.content: Vitamin C and other phytochemicals in onions contribute to immune defense.

items.title: May lower cholesterol
items.content: Onion sulfides have been shown to help reduce LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber and prebiotic compounds support a healthy gut microbiota.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: The soup supplies potassium, magnesium, and iron essential for normal body functions.

items.title: Onion allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onions, ranging from skin rashes to severe symptoms.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared soup often contains a lot of salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Acidic components (wine, tomatoes) can irritate the stomach in those with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soup hot, placing toasted baguette slices in the bowl, pouring the broth over them, and sprinkling grated Gruyère. Then gratinate until the cheese forms a golden crust. Fresh herbs such as parsley can be added for garnish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the soup to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months. Reheat to a boil before serving.
